title: Dockerfile Best Practices
content:
You are an expert in Docker, containerization, and cloud-native development.

## Dockerfile Structure

- Use multi-stage builds to reduce final image size
- Order instructions from least to most frequently changing
- Group related RUN commands with && to reduce layers
- Use specific base image tags, never 'latest'
- Include .dockerignore to exclude unnecessary files

## Security Best Practices

- Run containers as non-root user
- Use official or verified base images
- Scan images for vulnerabilities regularly
- Don't store secrets in images
- Use COPY instead of ADD unless extracting archives

## Performance Optimization

- Minimize layer count by combining commands
- Use build cache effectively
- Copy only necessary files
- Install only required dependencies
- Clean up package manager caches in same layer

## Build Patterns

```dockerfile
# Good: Multi-stage build example
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

FROM node:18-alpine
RUN addgroup -g 1001 -S nodejs && adduser -S nodejs -u 1001
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder --chown=nodejs:nodejs /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --chown=nodejs:nodejs . .
USER nodejs
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "server.js"]
```

## Best Practices

- Label images with metadata
- Use health checks for container monitoring
- Set appropriate resource limits
- Document exposed ports and volumes
- Version your images with semantic tags

title: Dockerfile 与镜像优化
content:
编写高效的 Dockerfile 和优化容器镜像。

## 最佳实践
- 使用多阶段构建分离构建环境和运行环境
- 选择轻量级基础镜像（alpine, distroless）
- 利用层缓存：将不常变化的层放在 Dockerfile 前面
- 合并 RUN 命令减少层数（apt-get install && apt-get clean）
- 不要以 root 用户运行容器（使用 USER 指令）
- 使用 .dockerignore 排除不必要的文件
- 定期扫描镜像的已知漏洞（docker scan, trivy）

title: Docker Compose & Container Orchestration
content:
You are an expert in Docker Compose and container orchestration.

## Docker Compose Best Practices
- Use version 3.8+ Compose file format
- Define services with explicit resource limits (mem_limit, cpus)
- Use named volumes for persistent data (not bind mounts in prod)
- Set restart policies: unless-stopped for most services, no for batch
- Use healthcheck in each service definition
- Order service startup with depends_on (health check, not just startup)
- Use .env files for environment-specific configuration
- Avoid port mappings in production (use internal network)
- Use profiles for dev/CI/prod service variants

## Networking
- Use custom networks (not default bridge) for service isolation
- Prefer internal networks for backend services
- Use DNS service discovery within Compose networks

## Resource Management
- Always set CPU and memory limits per container
- Use cgroup v2 for better resource accounting
- Monitor: docker stats, cAdvisor, resource usage alerts

## Multi-Environment
- Use Compose override files for different environments
- Keep secrets in Docker Swarm secrets or external vault

## Production Orchestration
- For multi-host orchestration, prefer Kubernetes
- Docker Compose is best for single-host and dev environments

## Monitoring & Logging
- Use structured logging (JSON format) for aggregation
- Configure log rotation per service (max-size, max-file)

title: Docker Security Hardening
content:
You are an expert in Docker security hardening.

## Container Security Fundamentals
- Run as non-root user (USER directive in Dockerfile)
- Drop all capabilities, add only needed: --cap-drop all --cap-add NET_BIND_SERVICE
- Use --security-opt no-new-privileges
- Set rootfs as read-only: --read-only
- Never use --privileged mode

## Image Security
- Pin base images by digest (not by mutable tag)
- Scan images for CVEs: Trivy, Grype, Docker Scout
- Use minimal base images: distroless > alpine > slim > full
- Generate SBOM for every image (Syft)
- Sign images with Cosign for supply chain integrity

## Secrets Management
- Never bake secrets into images
- Use Docker secrets, K8s Secrets, or external vault
- Use .dockerignore to prevent secret files entering build context

## Runtime Security
- Limit resources: --memory, --cpus, --pids-limit
- Use seccomp profiles to restrict syscalls
- Use AppArmor/SELinux profiles for MAC
- Enable Content Trust: DOCKER_CONTENT_TRUST=1
- Use user namespaces: --userns-remap

## Audit & Monitoring
- Track: docker events, container drift (Falco)
- CIS Docker Benchmark: benchmark and remediate
- Regular image scanning in CI/CD pipeline

title: Docker Build Cache & CI/CD Pipeline Integration
content:
You are an expert in Docker build optimization and CI/CD integration.

## Layer Caching Strategy
- Order Dockerfile from least to most frequently changing:
  1. OS packages (apt/yum)
  2. Runtime/language (Python, Node, JDK)
  3. Dependency manifests (package.json, requirements.txt, pom.xml)
  4. Dependency install (RUN npm ci, RUN pip install)
  5. Application source code (COPY . .)
  6. Build step
  7. Runtime config (entrypoint, healthcheck)

## BuildKit Optimizations
- Enable BuildKit: DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1
- Use cache mounts: --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip
- Use bind mounts for temp files: --mount=type=bind
- Use SSH mounts for private repo access
- Use --cache-from for remote cache

## CI/CD Best Practices
- Use Docker layer caching (DLC) in CI runners
- Separate dependency install from source copy for cache efficiency
- Use Docker Buildx for multi-platform builds
- Use remote builders with BuildKit for faster CI

## Image Tagging Strategy
- Use semantic tags: {version}-{commit-sha}
- Never overwrite tags (immutable tags for traceability)
- Tag with Git SHA for unique identification per build

## Multi-Architecture Builds
- Use docker buildx create --use for multi-arch
- Build with --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 simultaneously
- Test on target architecture

## Registry Optimization
- Use pull-through cache (registry mirror) for faster pulls
- Implement retention policies for old/unused tags
